interactions.title: Brunnar’s account of Dhrukmir
lines: DM: You learned from talking to Brunnar, the stone giant, that Dhrukmir, Dhrukmir, Skybreaker, king of the Giants in this region, is a Chalyte-obsessed creature who has modified himself and the land around him, powered by the Chalyte he— his ogre servants mine from a giant pit mine beneath the tower.

DM: Now it is said he can grow to be 70 feet tall and destroy people with his club of crystalline Chalyte, and you are gonna go kill him, neutralize him, convince him not to be quite so evil and authoritarian.
Delwath: Now I think we're going to kill him.

before: DM: So.

DM: On Vindristjarna, as the sun rises after you returned late last night via Teleport, following a long— a medium, enlightening conversation with an ogre who believed that Kenzo was a magic rock and a shorter but more informative conversation with disaffected stone giant.

DM: You now find yourself preparing on the deck of Vindristjarna, about 30 miles away from the Thundercrown, the Riftstone Gorge and the Hanging Tower, anchored by bridges of lightning to 2 mountains from which the massive, Chalyte-powered death ray vaporizes anybody who comes close.
Kenzo: Fuck. I forgot about all this shit.
after: DM: You have arrived here with 2 of the servants of the magistrate: Octavia Antussus, a middle-aged woman in her early fifties. From speaking to her on the journey, you hear she served as a bodyguard and military tutor for the magistrate when he was growing up, and she has come, because should you succeed in somehow dislodging the 70 foot tall giant and his massive death ray, she is prepared to go to the nearby city of Argento, take control of the legions there and march them to claim the Chalyte mine for the magistrate, which is, after all, the reason you're here in the first place.

DM: You've also traveled with Tristan Brighteyes, a young windcaller who reports to Tiberius, excited about the idea of being part of this mission, and your craziness, ability to tackle things that seem like they would kill ordinary folk. However, you'd like to put it, he is impressed with you.

DM: But he is here also, because he has spells to magically communicate back with the magistrate, report the events as they happen. And so, as you gather on the deck of Vindristjarna, looking out across the dry, windswept foothills of the Chataan mountains, preparing with Seeker and simulacrum Seeker 3 standing together, ready to teleport, arguing over who is gonna cast Teleport. Seeker, of course, never having failed to teleport anybody anywhere except in the Feywild. But that doesn't count.
Delwath: Fair enough, we're going to the top of the—to the entrance.
